references.text: The warning to stay away from the banned thing (cherem) so as not to be banned oneself, parallel to the warning in Deuteronomy 7:26 about bringing abominations into the house.
Achan's sin illustrates the consequence of breaking the command in Deuteronomy 7:26 by taking what is banned.
Israel's breach of the covenant by taking from the banned things, which directly shows the consequence of ignoring the warning in Deuteronomy 7:26.
The same terminology regarding the banned thing (cherem) and God's wrath, connected with idolatry.
Use of the word 'abomination' (toevah) in connection with pagan practices that Israel must avoid.
The link between idolatry and what is abominable, focusing on separating oneself from pagan practices.
The contrast between fearing the Lord and hating evil, reflecting the principle of detesting idols.
Paul applies the principle of not bringing abominations into God's temple, parallel to the warning about not bringing them into the house.
In the new Jerusalem nothing unclean or abominable will enter, reflecting the principle from Deuteronomy 7:26.
